investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately marked Unschedulable and remains stuck until the eval timeout fires. Because no pod ever starts, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completes, the evidence object stays empty, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval environment's production-api cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with preemption also exhausted.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141747 confirms the pod was stuck for ~137s before the eval timed out, consistent with the scheduler message.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner never reached the VM allocation or agent creation step.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=151717, empty evidenceKeys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, latencyMs=147283, empty evidenceKeys.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod never schedules, this call never resolves and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the cluster cannot expand scheduling to non-kata nodes even as a fallback. Preemption is also blocked because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 kata nodes.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or a concurrent workload may have left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 kata nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower confidence: The node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 nodes could indicate a misconfiguration in the pod spec (e.g., a label or taint that was recently changed), but the scheduler message treats this as a separate constraint from the resource exhaustion, and no source change evidence points to a pod spec modification.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available (allocatable > 0) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not request kata.peerpods.io/vm at all, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a node affinity misconfiguration is the sole blocker).

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the 4 nodes with affinity mismatch are shown to have available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the node affinity/selector misconfiguration — not resource exhaustion — would be the primary blocker.
If no orphaned remote-agent pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the exhaustion is caused by legitimate concurrent workloads rather than a cleanup failure in the eval runner.

Add a node-affinity conformance eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the required labels/selectors for remote-agent scheduling, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable node pool.

Introduce a latency-band eval for remote-agent pod scheduling specifically (time from pod submission to Running state), with a tighter warning threshold than the full remote-agent-create check, to detect capacity pressure earlier.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity exhausted on production Kubernetes cluster — all three remote-agent checks unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run because every pod the eval attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and node-affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the runner could not produce any evidence, leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering the contract-gap failure.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: the scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) shows that the 2 nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot free any. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion that prevents the eval runner from creating a remote agent pod at all; the contract-gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence) is a downstream consequence of the pod never starting, not an independent code defect. This is an eval-layer signal of a production infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 145s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151717, status=fail — the check ran for ~152 s, well past the 145 s unschedulable window, confirming the pod never progressed.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler rejection message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=141747, status=fail — the create step failed for the same infrastructure reason before remote-agent-state was even attempted.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, latencyMs=147283, status=fail — the runtime check also could not schedule a pod.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent because the pod never started and the runner never reached the API calls that would populate them.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905 — this is the call that triggers pod scheduling; if scheduling fails, no subsequent evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires ['orgId','agentId','readyState','state'] — none were produced, confirming the runner never advanced past pod creation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing peer-pod VMs that have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free slots.

[Likely contributing] The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements for the remote-agent workload, so the effective scheduling pool is limited to exactly 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

[Possible] A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in the runner failed or was interrupted), leaving VM slots occupied and unavailable for subsequent runs.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A quota or limit on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was recently lowered, reducing the number of schedulable VMs below the concurrent demand from eval runs plus production traffic. No quota-change evidence is present in this packet.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the root cause would not be resource exhaustion and an alternative (e.g., node affinity misconfiguration, API-level failure, or runner bug) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded and produced all four required evidence fields, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity problem.
If only remote-agent-state failed while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime passed, the cause would be localized to the state-polling logic rather than shared pod-scheduling infrastructure.

If the scheduler message were absent and the pod reached a running state but the runner still returned empty evidence, the root cause would shift to a runner code defect or API response parsing issue in run-status-probes.mjs rather than infrastructure capacity.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, so capacity exhaustion is surfaced as a distinct infrastructure check rather than a downstream contract-gap failure.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector requirements, alerting when the eligible pool shrinks below a safe threshold.
Add a historical trend eval for remote-agent-state latency to detect gradual capacity degradation (increasing scheduling wait times) before full exhaustion occurs.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 03:23 and 03:28 UTC on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime response contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was never satisfied.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never launched, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned an agent, and zero evidence fields were produced — causing a total contract gap against the 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message). This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster's kata/peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

All three sibling checks hit the same constraint within a ~5-minute window, consistent with sustained pool exhaustion rather than a transient blip.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If the cluster was recently scaled or nodes were replaced/relabeled, the eligible node count may have shrunk, reducing the effective VM capacity ceiling.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level capacity under-provisioning: with only 2 nodes eligible for kata peer-pod workloads and no preemption victims available, the cluster has no headroom to absorb concurrent eval runs or other remote agent workloads. This is a capacity planning concern rather than a code defect.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever allocated, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is immediately marked Unschedulable and remains stuck until the eval timeout fires. Because no pod ever starts, the createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never completes, the evidence object stays empty, and all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is scoped to the eval environment's production-api cluster. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with preemption also exhausted.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=141747 confirms the pod was stuck for ~137s before the eval timed out, consistent with the scheduler message.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}), confirming the runner never reached the VM allocation or agent creation step.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm', '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=151717, empty evidenceKeys.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, latencyMs=147283, empty evidenceKeys.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the pod never schedules, this call never resolves and no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion can be evaluated when evidence is empty.
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes in the production-api cluster, leaving zero capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary: The 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, meaning the cluster cannot expand scheduling to non-kata nodes even as a fallback. Preemption is also blocked because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 kata nodes.

Tertiary: A prior eval run or a concurrent workload may have left orphaned remote-agent VMs running on the 2 kata nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them. The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to release resources, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots could remain occupied.

Lower confidence: The node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 nodes could indicate a misconfiguration in the pod spec (e.g., a label or taint that was recently changed), but the scheduler message treats this as a separate constraint from the resource exhaustion, and no source change evidence points to a pod spec modification.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available (allocatable > 0) on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the failure, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If the pod spec for remote-agent pods does not request kata.peerpods.io/vm at all, the scheduler message would indicate a different root cause (e.g., a node affinity misconfiguration is the sole blocker).

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all required evidence, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained exhaustion condition.
If the 4 nodes with affinity mismatch are shown to have available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the node affinity/selector misconfiguration — not resource exhaustion — would be the primary blocker.
If no orphaned remote-agent pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, the exhaustion is caused by legitimate concurrent workloads rather than a cleanup failure in the eval runner.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity' failure rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add an orphan-detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations and alerts if any have been running beyond the expected eval lifecycle window, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node-affinity conformance eval that verifies the expected number of nodes carry the required labels/selectors for remote-agent scheduling, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable node pool.

Introduce a latency-band eval for remote-agent pod scheduling specifically (time from pod submission to Running state), with a tighter warning threshold than the full remote-agent-create check, to detect capacity pressure earlier.

investigations.title: Remote Agents eval failure: kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity exhausted on production Kubernetes cluster — all three remote-agent checks unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the same eval run because every pod the eval attempted to schedule was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and node-affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes. Because no pod ever reached a running state, the runner could not produce any evidence, leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) absent and triggering the contract-gap failure.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: the scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) shows that the 2 nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot free any. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion that prevents the eval runner from creating a remote agent pod at all; the contract-gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence) is a downstream consequence of the pod never starting, not an independent code defect. This is an eval-layer signal of a production infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader user-facing outage.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler reports '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — pod was stuck unscheduled for 145s before the eval timed out.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=151717, status=fail — the check ran for ~152 s, well past the 145 s unschedulable window, confirming the pod never progressed.

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduler rejection message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'), latencyMs=141747, status=fail — the create step failed for the same infrastructure reason before remote-agent-state was even attempted.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler rejection message, latencyMs=147283, status=fail — the runtime check also could not schedule a pod.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent because the pod never started and the runner never reached the API calls that would populate them.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1905 — this is the call that triggers pod scheduling; if scheduling fails, no subsequent evidence can be written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: the remote-agent-state contract at line 264 requires ['orgId','agentId','readyState','state'] — none were produced, confirming the runner never advanced past pod creation.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing peer-pod VMs that have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to free slots.

[Likely contributing] The 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements for the remote-agent workload, so the effective scheduling pool is limited to exactly 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

[Possible] A prior eval run or production workload created remote-agent VMs that were not cleaned up (e.g., withCleanup in the runner failed or was interrupted), leaving VM slots occupied and unavailable for subsequent runs.

[Possible but unconfirmed] A quota or limit on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was recently lowered, reducing the number of schedulable VMs below the concurrent demand from eval runs plus production traffic. No quota-change evidence is present in this packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 03:23 and 03:28 UTC on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected, meaning the agent pod never started and the runtime response contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was never satisfied.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144 seconds until the eval timed out. Because the pod never launched, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned an agent, and zero evidence fields were produced — causing a total contract gap against the 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message). This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint in the production Kubernetes cluster's kata/peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: both nodes that carry this resource reported Insufficient capacity, meaning all available VM slots were occupied by other workloads at the time of the eval run. All three sibling checks hit the same constraint within a ~5-minute window, consistent with sustained pool exhaustion rather than a transient blip.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If the cluster was recently scaled or nodes were replaced/relabeled, the eligible node count may have shrunk, reducing the effective VM capacity ceiling.

TERTIARY — Cluster-level capacity under-provisioning: with only 2 nodes eligible for kata peer-pod workloads and no preemption victims available, the cluster has no headroom to absorb concurrent eval runs or other remote agent workloads. This is a capacity planning concern rather than a code defect.

UNLIKELY — Eval runner misconfiguration: the runner branch at run-status-probes.mjs line 1913-1918 is correctly structured and the token guard at line 1915 was not triggered (the check ran, not skipped). The failure is upstream of the runner logic.

Investigate whether other workloads (non-eval remote agents or other peer-pod consumers) are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots that prevented the eval pods from scheduling. If so, assess whether resource quotas or priority classes should be applied.
Consider adding more nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or increasing the VM slot count on existing eligible nodes if the pool is consistently at capacity during eval windows.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184). Prioritize restoring scheduling capacity for the required checks first.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A re-run of the eval that succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) would indicate the scheduling failure was transient and the pool has since recovered.

Kubernetes node inspection showing that kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity was not exhausted at the time of the failure would suggest the scheduler message was misleading or the pod had an incorrect resource request.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., targeting a non-existent label) and that all 6 nodes actually have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity would shift the root cause from pool exhaustion to selector misconfiguration.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same timestamp would indicate the failure was isolated to the runtime check rather than a shared infrastructure constraint — but both siblings also failed (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state), making this unlikely.
User-traffic or incident signals showing no impact on real remote agent provisioning would confirm this is an eval-only infrastructure issue and not a user-facing outage.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval that directly checks kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity (allocatable vs. allocated) before attempting remote agent creation, so pool exhaustion is surfaced as its own signal rather than a downstream scheduling timeout.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check eval that submits a dry-run pod with the remote agent's node selector and resource requests, reporting the scheduler's decision without actually launching an agent. This would catch Unschedulable conditions earlier and with lower cost.

Add a historical trend eval that tracks remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime pass/fail rates over time to detect recurring exhaustion windows and distinguish transient from sustained capacity issues.

Add a sibling-correlation eval rule: when all checks under a feature share the same Unschedulable message pattern, auto-escalate to a shared-infrastructure-dependency alert rather than treating each check as an independent failure.
